examples.en: Wearing leather clothes in winter keeps you warm.
Leather clothes are hard to take care of if they get rained on.
My father still wears his old leather clothes.
The leather clothes were too heavy, so I didn't buy them.
I bought a jacket at a leather clothing shop.

examples.ko: 가죽옷은 집에서 빨지 말고 세탁소에 맡기세요.
examples.en: Don't wash leather clothes at home. Take them to the cleaner's.

explain: 가죽으로 만든 옷을 통틀어 말해요. 구체적인 옷은 '가죽 재킷', '가죽 바지'처럼 가죽을 앞에 붙여 말해요. 관리는 보통 '세탁소에 맡기다'고 해요.
explain_en: It is a general word for clothes made of leather. For a specific item, people put '가죽' in front, like '가죽 재킷' or '가죽 바지'. For care, people usually say '세탁소에 맡기다' (leave it at the cleaner's).

examples.en: I stared at a screen all night, so my eyes feel dry and scratchy.

examples.ko: 생선의 눈알을 보면 신선한지 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can tell whether a fish is fresh by looking at its eyes.
The eyes of cartoon characters are very big.
I just rolled my eyes around, pretending not to know.

examples.ko: 인형 눈알 하나가 떨어져서 다시 붙였어요.
examples.en: One of the doll's eyes fell off, so I glued it back.
I made a snowman with no eyes and no nose.

explain: '눈'은 보는 기능이나 얼굴 부위 전체까지 가리키지만, '눈알'은 동그란 안구 부분만 가리켜요. 인형, 생선, 만화의 눈 모양을 말할 때 자연스러워요. 사람의 눈은 보통 '눈'이라고 하고, '눈알'은 거친 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: 눈 can mean the face part or the ability to see, but 눈알 points only to the round eyeball. It is natural for dolls, fish, and cartoon eyes. For a person's eyes, people normally say 눈; 눈알 can sound rough.

examples.en: In summer I go out wearing a straw hat.
My straw hat blew away in the wind.
A straw hat is nice because it blocks the sun.
I attached a ribbon to the straw hat.
I bought a straw hat at the beach.
I packed a straw hat and put on sunscreen too.

explain: 밀의 짚으로 엮어 만든 모자예요. 농부가 밭일할 때나 여름 바닷가에서 햇빛을 가리려고 많이 써요. 모자를 머리에 올리는 동작은 '쓰다'예요.
explain_en: It is a hat woven from wheat straw. Farmers wear it in the fields, and people wear it at the beach in summer to block the sun. The verb for putting on a hat is '쓰다'.

examples.en: In summer I wear an anklet and sandals.
The anklet was pretty, so I bought one more.
An anklet is less noticeable than a bracelet.
I also bought an anklet that matches my friend's.
I tried adding some style with a small anklet.
The anklet strap broke, so I bought a new one.

explain: '팔찌'는 손목에, '발찌'는 발목에 차요. 뉴스에 나오는 '전자발찌'는 위치를 확인하는 장치라서 장신구와는 쓰임이 아주 달라요.
explain_en: A 팔찌 goes on the wrist and a 발찌 goes on the ankle. The 전자발찌 you hear about in the news is a device that tracks location, so it is very different from jewelry.

examples.en: My child left the shoe bag at school.
You have to take your indoor shoes in a shoe bag.
It is dangerous to swing your shoe bag while walking.

examples.ko: 엄마가 아이 신발주머니에 이름을 써 줬어요.
examples.en: Mom wrote the child's name on the shoe bag.
The shoe bag got dirty, so I washed it in the washing machine.

examples.ko: 새 학기에 맞춰 신발주머니를 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a new shoe bag for the new school term.

explain: 학교에서 신는 실내화를 넣어 다니는 작은 주머니를 말할 때 자주 써요. '실내화 주머니'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is often used for the small bag that carries indoor shoes worn at school. It is also called '실내화 주머니'.

examples.ko: 그는 말할 때 아래턱을 앞으로 내미는 버릇이 있어요.
examples.en: He has a habit of pushing his lower jaw forward when he talks.
I had an X-ray of my lower jaw taken at the dentist.
My lower jaw hurts, so it is hard to eat.

examples.ko: 아래턱을 움직이며 천천히 씹어야 소화가 잘돼요.
examples.en: You digest better if you chew slowly, moving your lower jaw.

examples.ko: 하품을 크게 했더니 아래턱이 빠질 것 같았어요.
examples.en: I yawned so wide that my lower jaw felt like it would pop out.

examples.ko: 아래턱 선이 갸름해서 인상이 날카로워 보여요.
examples.en: The line of his lower jaw is slim, so he looks sharp.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '위턱'이에요. 일상에서는 보통 그냥 '턱'이라고 하고, 치과나 병원에서 위아래를 나눌 때 '아래턱'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '위턱' (upper jaw). In daily life people usually just say '턱', and '아래턱' is used when distinguishing top from bottom, such as at the dentist or hospital.

examples.en: My lower lip turned blue from the cold.
I have a habit of biting my lower lip when I'm nervous.

examples.ko: 김 씨가 아랫입술을 비죽이 내밀고 저를 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: Mr. Kim pushed out his lower lip and looked at me.
I hurt my lower lip when I fell, and it bled.

examples.ko: 아랫입술이 터져서 밥 먹을 때 아파요.
examples.en: My lower lip is cracked, so it hurts when I eat.

examples.ko: 자기 전에 아랫입술에 립밤을 듬뿍 발랐어요.
examples.en: I put a lot of lip balm on my lower lip before bed.

explain: 반대말은 '윗입술'이에요. 삐졌거나 울 것 같을 때 '아랫입술을 내밀다', 참거나 긴장할 때 '아랫입술을 깨물다'처럼 표정이나 버릇을 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '윗입술' (upper lip). It often appears in expressions of mood or habit, such as '아랫입술을 내밀다' when sulking, or '아랫입술을 깨물다' when holding back or feeling tense.

examples.ko: 얼굴색이 안 좋아 보이는데 어디 아파요?
examples.en: You look pale, are you sick somewhere?
When I put on makeup, my complexion gets much brighter.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 얼굴색을 환하게 만들어 줘요.
examples.en: This outfit makes my complexion look bright.

examples.ko: 그 소식을 듣고 얼굴색이 확 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: His face changed color when he heard the news.
I got a lot of sun, so my complexion changed.
I chose a lipstick that matches my skin tone.

explain: 건강이나 기분이 드러나는 얼굴의 색을 말해요. '얼굴색이 안 좋다'는 아프거나 피곤해 보인다는 걱정의 말로 자주 써요. 화장품이나 옷 이야기에서는 피부 톤을 뜻하기도 해요.
explain_en: It means the color of the face, which shows health or mood. '얼굴색이 안 좋다' is often said out of concern when someone looks sick or tired. In talk about cosmetics or clothes, it can also mean skin tone.

examples.en: The princess wore a sparkling crown.
The crown looks too heavy.
The crown was decorated with gold and jewels.
There were many people in front of the crown at the museum.
Jewels are set in the crown.
She received a crown and prize money at the pageant.

explain: 머리에 쓰니까 '왕관을 쓰다'라고 해요. 왕의 자리 자체는 '왕위'나 '왕좌'라고 불러서 물건인 '왕관'과 구분해요.
explain_en: Because it sits on the head, you say '왕관을 쓰다'. The position of king itself is '왕위' or '왕좌', which is separate from the object, the '왕관'.

examples.en: At home I wear comfortable everyday clothes.

examples.ko: 이 원피스는 일상복으로 입기에 딱 좋아요.
examples.en: This dress is just right to wear day to day.

examples.ko: 일상복 브랜드에서 세일을 해서 티셔츠를 샀어요.
examples.en: An everyday-wear brand was on sale, so I bought a T-shirt.

examples.ko: 출근할 때도 일상복 차림으로 다녀도 돼요?
examples.en: Is it okay to go to work in everyday clothes too?

examples.ko: 한복을 일상복처럼 입는 사람도 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More people are wearing hanbok like everyday clothes.

examples.ko: 일상복이 너무 낡아서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: My everyday clothes are so worn out that I need to buy new ones.

explain: '평상복'과 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요. 반대로 격식 있는 자리의 옷은 '정장'이나 '예복'이라고 해요. 한복을 평소에 입기 편하게 만든 옷은 '생활한복'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: It is used almost the same as '평상복' (casual wear). The opposite is formal wear such as '정장' or '예복'. Hanbok redesigned for daily comfort is called '생활한복'.

examples.en: In summer I often wear hot pants at home.

examples.ko: 그 핫팬츠가 너무 짧은 것 같아요.
examples.en: Those hot pants seem too short.
I wore a long T-shirt with the hot pants.
Hot pants are too cold to wear in winter, right?

examples.ko: 동생이 핫팬츠 한 벌을 사 왔어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling bought a pair of hot pants.
I cut my jeans and made them into hot pants.

explain: 매우 짧은 반바지를 말해요. 길이가 보통인 바지는 '반바지'라고 하고, 몸에 붙고 아주 짧은 것을 '핫팬츠'라고 구별해 써요. 옷을 셀 때는 '한 벌'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means extremely short shorts. Ordinary shorts are called '반바지', and '핫팬츠' is used for the very short, fitted kind. Use '한 벌' to count them.

examples.ko: 눈 흰자위에 핏줄이 생겨서 안과에 갔어요.
examples.en: Blood vessels appeared in the white of my eye, so I went to the eye doctor.

examples.ko: 흰자위가 보일 만큼 눈을 크게 떴어요.
examples.en: I opened my eyes so wide that the whites showed.
A baby's eyes have clear, clean whites.

examples.ko: 삶은 달걀의 흰자위만 먹으면 칼로리가 낮아요.
examples.en: If you eat only the white of a boiled egg, the calories are low.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 화가 나면 흰자위를 번뜩이며 쳐다봐요.
examples.en: When that actor gets angry, he stares with the whites of his eyes flashing.
The color difference between the dark part and the white of the eye is clear.

explain: 눈 이야기에서는 '검은자위'와 짝으로 자주 나와요. 달걀 이야기에서는 보통 '흰자'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: In talk about eyes it often pairs with '검은자위' (the dark part). When talking about eggs, people usually say '흰자' more.
